title: Figma Make Kits: npm Packages, Library Variables, and Guidelines
content:
# Figma Make Kits

Make kits "enable teams to jump straight into building designs and prototypes in Make that are realistic to how your product looks and functions without having to add code and style context from scratch."

Rolled out to all paid plans beginning March 26, 2026; announced April 2, 2026. Guidance older than roughly Q1 2026 describing Figma Make as design-system-blind is stale.

## Three content types

1. **npm packages** — providing code context
2. **Variables and styles** — imported from published Figma Design libraries
3. **Guidelines** — instructions helping Make understand how to use system assets

This tri-partite structure is the distinguishing feature versus every other AI generator: **Figma is the only tool that can pull design tokens directly from the design source of truth** (published library variables) *and* the production component code (npm), and reconcile them with prose guidelines. Every other tool derives tokens from code only.

## Creation workflow

1. Start a new kit (assemble existing resources or build from scratch)
2. Add npm packages and/or library styles
3. Configure custom settings if needed
4. Write guidelines (critical for accurate results)
5. Test the kit thoroughly
6. Publish to organization via the "Publish kit" button

Guidelines require special attention for: explaining token quirks, organizing decisions logically, documenting typography completely, establishing color token hierarchy, stating constraints, and providing code composition examples. The emphasis on "token quirks" and "color token hierarchy" is telling — Figma acknowledges that raw variable export is insufficient and semantic intent must be written out in prose.

## Availability

Full seats on paid plans only. Organization admins approve and enable kits organization-wide. An individual design systems engineer cannot self-serve a private kit.

## Documented limitations — the important ones

- Kits cannot live in drafts; they must be relocated before publishing.
- **"Variable syntax extraction is simplified to CSS format, not preserved 1:1."** Your Figma variable structure does not survive intact.
- **"Only a subset of variables converts to global CSS values."** Not every Figma variable makes it into the generated style context. Multi-mode, aliased, or scoped variables are the likely casualties; expect to reconcile manually or document gaps in guidelines.

## Make attachments

Alongside kits, Make attachments bring project-specific context into prompts: PDFs, markdown, CSV/JSON datasets, screenshots, brand guidelines, legal copy, images, SVGs.

The stated problem: without them, designers summarized constraints verbally, producing idealized rather than production-ready prototypes. Attachments mean "real values reveal layout constraints and edge cases surface earlier" — an underrated capability, since feeding real data shapes makes generated components handle overflow, long strings, and empty states rather than the idealized three-word labels LLMs default to.

## The prototype-to-production claim

Figma documents a closed loop no other tool claims: build in Make against the real production package, then "deploy your Figma Make to production, using your production design system, using the Figma MCP Server." Prototype and production consume the identical package.
